indicator: Cocaine seized at ports (kg)
bias_limitations: Driven by enforcement effort and by route shifts (Antwerp, smaller ports, split loads). Falling seizures do not mean a smaller market. HARC and Douane totals count differently.
dataset_columns: c01_seized_harc_rotterdam_kg; c01_seized_schiphol_kg; c01_seized_douane_maritime_kg; c01_seized_douane_total_kg; c01_seizures_douane_total_n; c01_seizures_douane_maritime_n

indicator: Number of seizures and investigations started (HARC)
cocaine_specific: Partly (all drugs, cocaine split for kg)
example_values: Seizures 189 (2024), 172 (2025); investigations 80 → 55 (Rotterdam)
bias_limitations: Measures police activity more than the market.

indicator: Uithalers (people retrieving drugs from containers) apprehended
example_values: 284, 415, 261, 452, 266 (2020–2024); 83 (Jan–Oct 2025). OM counts 226 for Rotterdam 2024: different definition
bias_limitations: Enforcement-dependent; mostly Rotterdam; the drop in 2025 coincides with fewer seizures and more fencing/controls.

indicator: Minors / under-22s among uithalers
source: OM / HARC; CBS longread on characteristics
example_values: 2025 Rotterdam: 18 minors (youngest 13); 58% under 22
bias_limitations: Small numbers; depends on who gets caught.

indicator: Murder/manslaughter in the criminal milieu
bias_limitations: Small n; drug attribution only pooled, not per year; police classification of 'criminal milieu'. Ask police for yearly drug split.

indicator: Liquidations (planned killings)
bias_limitations: As C05. Strong downward trend while seizures rose: good example of market size ≠ harm.

indicator: Victims of murder/manslaughter by context
bias_limitations: Check whether a 'criminal milieu' context series is published. Not drug-specific.

indicator: Attacks with explosives (incl. attempts)
source: Politie / Offensief tegen Explosies; CBS maatwerk on suspects and victims
cocaine_specific: No (mix of drug conflicts, debts, personal feuds)
bias_limitations: Counting started recently; definition widened over time; drug link not recorded. Possibly a cocaine-market spillover, but only partly.

indicator: Registered Opiumwet offences, hard drugs (List I)
cocaine_specific: No (List I = cocaine, heroin, XTC, amphetamine …)
example_values: 9,442 hard-drug incidents registered by police in 2024 (NDM factsheet)
bias_limitations: Pure enforcement measure. Not cocaine-specific. Change in police priority looks like change in crime.

indicator: Suspects, OM cases, convictions, sentences (Opiumwet hard drugs)
bias_limitations: Enforcement-driven; split by drug normally not available. May be obtainable by request to OM/WODC.

indicator: Published court rulings mentioning cocaine
bias_limitations: Only a small, non-random share of rulings is published (serious and appealed cases over-represented). Gives quantities, sentences, roles, but not prevalence.

indicator: Closures of premises under Art. 13b Opiumwet
years: Per municipality; no national series found
bias_limitations: No national series; mostly cannabis-related and drug-dealing premises; policy-driven.

indicator: Monitor Georganiseerde Criminaliteit (6th round: cocaine smuggling and liquidations)
example_values: 16 recent cases; ~200 cases since 1997
bias_limitations: Not a time series; case selection. Useful for interpreting trends and choosing indicators.

indicator: GI-TOC Global Organized Crime Index: cocaine trade score, Netherlands
source: Global Initiative against Transnational Organized Crime
example_values: Cocaine trade 7.50 (2023) → 8.00 (2025); for comparison synthetic drugs 8.00, cannabis 5.50, heroin 4.00 (2025). 2021 score not retrieved
bias_limitations: Only three points; expert judgement; calibration across countries. Good validation for a register-based index and for country comparison.

indicator: Cocaine trade value in national accounts (illegal economy)
years: 2021 (estimates of illegal activities since the 2014 revision)
example_values: €10.7 bn earned within NL borders, €1.2 bn value added to NL GDP (2021)
bias_limitations: Model-based; market size, not harm. Check whether CBS has multiple years.

indicator: Perceived drug nuisance / drug dealing in neighbourhood
example_values: 2019: about a quarter of residents see drug use or dealing in their neighbourhood. 2025: new question on suspicious situations (49% saw at least one; drug dealing among the most named)
bias_limitations: Perception, not drug-specific; mostly street dealing and cannabis. The question set changed in 2025, which breaks the series.

indicator: Seizure counts and quantities reported to the EU
source: EUDA Statistical Bulletin; EUDA/Europol EU Drug Markets: Cocaine
bias_limitations: Same enforcement bias as C01, but harmonised: useful for country comparison.

indicator: Retail price per gram and purity
bias_limitations: Lower price and higher purity point to more supply. Not harm by itself, but an input to market size.

indicator: Payment-code fraud and insider cases at terminals
bias_limitations: Few points; reflects detection and new security measures.

indicator: Last-year cocaine use, adults 18+
access: Open (NDM, StatLine); microdata via CBS remote access
bias_limitations: Self-report; misses heavy and marginalised users; use is not the same as harm.

indicator: Last-month (and possibly weekly) cocaine use
source: Same survey (LSM-A); weekly use likely only in microdata
access: Last-month published; weekly via CBS microdata (to check)
example_values: More than a third of last-year users also used last month
bias_limitations: Your proposed 'weekly use' definition may need microdata. Small cells.

indicator: Lifetime cocaine use, pupils 12–16
example_values: Lifetime use, pupils 12–16: 2.0% (2003), 1.5 (2007), 1.4 (2011), 1.3 (2015), 1.1 (2019), 1.4 (2023). Corrected: an earlier summary had the direction reversed
bias_limitations: Few points; school-based (misses dropouts).

indicator: Nightlife survey: use, wish to cut back/stop
years: Grote Uitgaansonderzoek rounds incl. 2020 and 2023; Antenne club/festival survey 2017, 2022
example_values: Antenne: 22% of Amsterdam club/festival visitors used cocaine in the last 4 weeks (2022), similar to five years earlier
bias_limitations: Convenience sample; not comparable over rounds without care.

indicator: Clients in addiction care with cocaine as primary problem (powder vs crack)
access: Open (PDF); yearly values saved in ladis_cocaine_2016_2025.csv
example_values: Clients with cocaine as primary problem, all institutions: 6,383 (2016) → 8,215 (2024) → 7,788 (2025). Institutions reporting every year: 6,389 (2016) → 7,126 (2019) → 6,216 (2025). About 6,600 more have cocaine as a secondary problem (2025). Of the cases where the type is known, about 60:40 powder vs crack
bias_limitations: The rise in the 'all institutions' series comes partly from new institutions joining; institutions reporting every year show a decline since 2019. Use the constant series for trends. Private clinics don't report. Treatment demand also reflects access and the care gap. Powder/crack type unknown for over half of clients.
status: Checked (yearly values read from the report's vector charts, ±5)

indicator: Cocaine-related drug incidents (first aid at events, ambulance, ED, forensic doctors)
years: Since 2009; cocaine shares by service shown for 2019–2024
example_values: Cocaine incidents, all services: 1,091 (2019), 696, 708, 996, 1,119, 916 (2024). At hospital EDs (MDI + LIS): ≈525 (2019), 395, 391, 444, 471, 418 (2024), derived from the 2024 report's breakdown by service
bias_limitations: Not nationally representative; participating sites change over time (report advises percentages, not counts); drug mostly self-reported.

indicator: Drug-related emergency department visits (national estimate)
bias_limitations: Sample of hospitals, extrapolated; substance coding often missing. Partly overlaps with H06, which already includes LIS hospitals.

indicator: Drug deaths (direct effects), cocaine-involved where coded
cocaine_specific: Yes (cocaine is a separate group in NDM/CBS figures)
example_values: Cocaine as cause: 24 deaths (2014) → 61 (2024); all direct drug deaths 123 → 378
bias_limitations: Cocaine often co-occurs with other substances; coding practice changes; cardiovascular deaths from cocaine are missed.

indicator: Hospital admissions with cocaine diagnosis (ICD-10 F14 / T40.5)
source: LBZ (Dutch Hospital Data), published on vzinfo.nl (RIVM)
example_values: 2023: ≈120 hospital admissions with cocaine as main diagnosis and ≈1,800 with cocaine as secondary diagnosis
bias_limitations: Coding quality; secondary diagnoses under-recorded.

indicator: Cocaine use disorder: prevalence, DALYs, deaths (Netherlands)
bias_limitations: Heavily modelled from sparse Dutch inputs; smooth trends; great for country comparison.
status: Exists; values to download from GBD Results tool

indicator: Cocaine residues in wastewater (mg/1,000 inhabitants/day)
example_values: Amsterdam, Utrecht, Eindhoven roughly doubled 2011 → 2023
bias_limitations: Consumption, not harm; includes tourists and commuters; city sample changes.

indicator: Purity and adulterants of cocaine samples (e.g. levamisole)
years: Since ~1990s; purity series in DIMS reports
example_values: Average purity 76% in 2025 (highest in ten years); about 59% (2014), 68% (2017), 69% (2020), 71% (2021), 74% (2022). Share of samples with adulterants 65% (2016) → 18% (2025)
bias_limitations: Self-selected samples from users who come to test. Higher purity means higher acute risk.

indicator: Poison centre consultations involving cocaine
bias_limitations: Calls by professionals; depends on how often they call.
status: Exists (RIVM/NVIC yearly reviews); cocaine figures still to extract

indicator: Drivers testing positive for cocaine
source: NFI (blood samples from police traffic checks)
example_values: 64,000+ blood samples; cocaine found in 15% of positive samples (pooled 2017–2023)
bias_limitations: Depends on how many checks the police run.

indicator: Estimate of high-risk crack users
source: Forthcoming study (announced by National Rapporteur on Addiction)
bias_limitations: Not yet available.

indicator: Antenne Amsterdam (trends in Amsterdam drug use)
source: Hogeschool van Amsterdam (Nabben & Benschop) for Jellinek Preventie
example_values: GGD Amsterdam: last-year cocaine use 10% of adults (2024), stable since 2016. Jellinek intake: cocaine third after alcohol and cannabis
bias_limitations: Amsterdam only; part qualitative; good for early signals and validation.

indicator: Purity and adulterants of police-seized street cocaine
example_values: 69.2% base on average (90 samples, latest round); NFI and DIMS trends match
bias_limitations: Small samples; police seizures, not a random draw. Useful as a check on DIMS (H12), which relies on self-selected samples.

indicator: Cocaine production/processing sites dismantled
bias_limitations: Enforcement-driven; small numbers.
